Buy a Canadian ID Card on Telegram

A Canadian id card sold on Telegram is either a replica, a registered original, or a genuine document with your details typed in. Those three are priced differently and fail differently, and the advert rarely says which.

Issuing authority
a provincial registry office
Observed price band
80–280 CAD
Typical delivery
3 to 21 days, tracked
Local name
provincial photo card
Document type
An ID card is a domestic identity document issued by a civil registry, police force or municipal office. It proves identity inside the country and usually nothing outside it.

buy canadian id card on telegram – the short version

If you want the short version, a Canadian id card bought through Telegram is only worth the money when three things line up. The stock has to match what a provincial registry office uses, the number has to follow that office format, and the seller has to survive a question about a feature a photocopier cannot copy.

Work through the rest of this page with the card in front of you if you can. The numbered process later on is the sequence to follow and the checks list is what to look for at each step.

Buy a ID Card via Telegram: how the transaction works

Ask for the issue date and the issuing office before you ask the price. A seller working with a provincial registry office stock answers instantly. A reseller has to go and look, and that pause tells you where you sit in the chain.

If the seller wants to move to another app for payment, that is normal, but keep the conversation on Telegram. The chat is the only record that survives a disappearing account.

Who actually issues a ID Card

In Canada the office behind the id card is a provincial registry office. The local name is provincial photo card. Use the local name in the chat and the seller immediately knows whether you have done any reading.

Register access varies. Some countries let you check a number online, some need the holder, some need a call. Ask the seller what route exists and expect a specific answer rather than a general one.

Replica or registered original

Replica and registered original are used interchangeably in adverts and they are not the same purchase. A replica is a print. It copies the layout and fails on UV, on substrate and on the number.

The failure modes are different too. A print fails the first UV torch. Stock fails the number. A registered original fails only if the entry has lapsed or the details do not match it.

What a fair price looks like

Observed adverts for a Canadian id card cluster between 80–280 CAD. That is the range to hold in your head, and it is deliberately wide because it covers three different products.

There is a floor below which the maths stops working for the seller. Below roughly the bottom third of the band, nobody is buying stock, so nobody is selling you stock.

The buying process, step by step

Follow these in sequence and stop at the first one that fails.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is a provincial registry office.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format a provincial registry office uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 80–280 CAD band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

These are the checks that separate a real Canadian id card from a good print. All of them are cheap to run and two are local to Canada.

  • Confirm the province is spelled and abbreviated correctly and that the card carries a provincial crest rather than a federal one.
  • Check the passport for maple leaf perforations and the raised intaglio feel of the coat of arms.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for a provincial registry office. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

These end a Canadian id card conversation for good.

  • A passport data page with the place of birth written in American state format.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

How much is an ID card on Telegram?

Between 90 and 500 US dollars. A print sits at the bottom, a chip card with a valid number at the top.

Is an ID card worth buying at all?

It is the cheapest document to fake convincingly, so it is also the one most often faked badly. Buy it only with a number check.

Do ID cards work abroad?

Inside the issuing country, yes. Outside it, most are only accepted as secondary evidence.

What is the giveaway on a fake ID?

The number. It is the one part that has to obey a rule, and sellers who invent numbers rarely know the rule.

Can I check an ID number myself?

In most countries yes, because the algorithm is published. Search for the country name and check digit.

Before you pay

Print the checklist, run it in order and pay only at the end. That is the whole method for a Canadian id card.
